name: Heavens to Betsy
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: Corin Tucker and Tracy Sawyer played the 1991 International Pop Underground Convention with, by Tucker's account, hardly a song written. They made one album, quit in 1994, and in 2026 played again after 32 years.

eras.title: Athens first, then a bluff in Olympia
eras.text: Corin Tucker and Tracy Sawyer met in middle school in Eugene, Oregon. A train trip to Athens, Georgia came first; a year later Tucker was at Evergreen in Olympia and the duo had a festival slot.

years.cap: Sawyer on bass at an early show
years.h: A train to Athens, Georgia, and a $100 drum kit
years.p: Between Tucker's college start and Sawyer's senior year, the two went on what Tucker called a "musical pilgrimage". Sawyer came home with a used kit.
years.xp:
Tucker had already come up with the name Heavens to Betsy that spring, according to Wikipedia. Her father gave her a guitar he built and an amp, and the two practiced at her parents' house.

In the 2018 Bandcamp Daily interview they say the drum kit was put together from parts for $100.

years.h: Their first show is Girl Night at the International Pop Underground Convention
years.p: Michelle Noel of KAOS radio invited Tucker to play the International Pop Underground Convention's opening-night Girl Night, and Tucker said yes. The duo played three songs.
years.xp:
The K Records festival in Olympia opened with an all-female bill, billed as Love Rock Revolution Girl Style Now, that is often cited as a turning point for riot grrrl.

Tucker told Bandcamp Daily she said yes "even though I don't think we'd even written a song."

eras.title: They tour by convoy, make one album, and quit
eras.text: K Records and Kill Rock Stars put out their records, and they toured in two cars linked by walkie-talkies. Calculated, the one full-length, came out in 1994, the year the band ended and Tucker started Sleater-Kinney.

years.cap: The 1992 demo cassette and its photocopied yellow j-card, Olympia
years.h: Molly Neuman records an eight-song tape at Evergreen
years.p: The [[Bratmobile|d6dfbc0b-d737-49df-be8e-517b85985bcb]] drummer cut it as a demo; K Records released it as a cassette. The master is missing, so it has never been reissued.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the tape was first meant as a demo and went out through K anyway. It is the band's first release, ahead of the Bratmobile split and the Kill Rock Stars 7-inch.

years.h: "My Secret" goes on a split 7-inch with Bratmobile
years.p: The two Olympia duos share a single on K Records, the label that gave Heavens to Betsy their first stage.

years.h: These Monsters Are Real comes out on Kill Rock Stars
years.p: Four songs on a 7-inch for Kill Rock Stars, remastered and reissued in 2018.
years.xp: Sources differ on the year: Wikipedia and Trouser Press say 1992, while the Bandcamp Daily piece says 1993.

years.h: In Bellingham, Tucker meets Carrie Brownstein of Excuse 17
years.p: A show in Washington brings Tucker together with [[Carrie Brownstein|2b7d41d8-21d4-4410-a57b-5ddaeb131094]], then at Western Washington University and playing in [[Excuse 17|bad37a2a-1ab8-4605-b8f3-e0615cd7de64]].

yt: "Me and Her", X-Ray Cafe, Portland, July 7, 1993
years.h: Two cars and a pair of walkie-talkies cover the US, then England
years.p: Sawyer, on the tour with [[Bratmobile|d6dfbc0b-d737-49df-be8e-517b85985bcb]]: "We went with two cars and got walkie-talkies." England came next.
years.xp:
Tucker, on the schedule: "It's a miracle we ever made any show even remotely on time." Wikipedia says a later national tour with Brownstein's [[Excuse 17|bad37a2a-1ab8-4605-b8f3-e0615cd7de64]] followed.

With no internet, the band booked shows by phoning venues and writing down directions by hand, as they described it to Bandcamp Daily.

years.h: Calculated gets four days in Seattle with John Goodmanson
years.p: The band produced itself; Goodmanson engineered the sessions.

years.h: Calculated arrives with an A minus from Robert Christgau
years.p: Twelve songs in 39 minutes 50 seconds on Kill Rock Stars, including Axemen and Waitress Hell.
years.xp:
Tucker plays guitar and sings; Sawyer drums and plays bass. Trouser Press heard anger, fear, confusion and vulnerability despite basic instrumental skills, with Tucker's wail set against Sawyer's screams.

Trouser Press dates the album to 1993. Wikipedia gives March 21, 1994, and says Rolling Stone later put it in its Riot Grrrl Album Guide.

yt: With Excuse 17, CBGB, New York, Aug 17, 1994
years.h: Tucker and Sawyer call it when the friendship starts to fray
years.p: They said the band ended as their friendship and the seriousness of the music pulled apart.
years.xp:
Tucker to Bandcamp Daily: "There's a maturity factor when you go from being children to being adults." Sawyer: "Our personalities started shifting. We sort of were becoming more distant."

Wikipedia lists Tucker's later bands as [[Sleater-Kinney|e36e78eb-3ace-4acd-882c-16789e700ab7]], Heartless Martin, Cadallaca, the Corin Tucker Band and Filthy Friends, and Sawyer's as Flying Tigers, The Lies and Motel No-Tell.

years.h: Tucker's next band is Sleater-Kinney, with Brownstein
years.p: [[Sleater-Kinney|e36e78eb-3ace-4acd-882c-16789e700ab7]] starts within months of the split; Trouser Press names Lora Macfarlane as its first drummer.

eras.title: Back after 32 years
eras.text: Their songs turned up in films and in the video game Gone Home. In 2026 the duo played again.

years.cap: Heavens to Betsy at the reunion show, Turn! Turn! Turn!, Portland, June 25, 2026
years.h: Heavens to Betsy play Portland for the first time in 32 years
years.p: A sold-out Turn! Turn! Turn! hears 18 songs, including Calculated and Axemen. A 10-date US tour starts October 17 in San Francisco.
years.xp: Stereogum reported the show was announced the day after. The tour runs through October and November 2026, with tickets on sale July 2.
